The challenge

What makes management & it consulting different.

01

Bid teams rewrite the same credentials, methods and team pages for every proposal.

02

Desk research takes analysts days, and AI shortcuts produce claims without reliable sources.

03

Status reporting across workstreams is manual, so slipping deliverables and budget burn surface late.

04

Utilization and pipeline figures differ by practice and are a month old when partners plan staffing.

05

Frameworks in past deliverables are hard to find for anyone outside the original team.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for management & it consulting.

01

Enquiry and RFP triage

Enquiries and RFP documents summarized into need, scope, deadline and evaluation criteria, matched to a practice and routed to a partner with a response clock and a go or no-go note.

02

Proposal library and drafting

Approved credentials, method pages and CVs retrieved by sector and service, then drafted into a first version that the bid lead rewrites and the partner prices.

03

Research packs with citations

Market, company and regulatory research where every claim links to its source with a retrieval date, conflicting evidence is shown side by side and gaps are marked for analysts.

04

Status reports across workstreams

Weekly drafts from Jira or Asana and time data, with risks, decisions needed and budget burn, edited by the engagement manager before the steering committee sees them.

05

Knowledge assistant over past deliverables

Frameworks, lessons learned and sanitized deliverables searchable with citations, with access limited by each client's confidentiality terms.

06

Utilization and pipeline dashboard

One agreed set of definitions for utilization, realization and weighted pipeline, refreshed daily in Power BI, with individual detail visible only to managers.

Enquiry and first responseStarter2–3 weeks

Enquiry capture, qualification and routing

Every new enquiry from forms, email, WhatsApp or referrals becomes one CRM record with a short AI summary, a suggested service line and a named owner, so prospects get a prompt and relevant reply.

Marketing & creative agencies · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Agency and consulting enquiries arrive in founders' inboxes, personal WhatsApp and LinkedIn messages. Some wait days for a reply, others get a proposal before anyone checks budget, timing or fit, and nobody can see which sources bring work worth winning.

Trigger

A website or Typeform enquiry is submitted, a prospect messages the firm's WhatsApp Business number, or a referral or RFP email arrives in the shared new-business inbox.

How it runs

  • Create or update the contact and company in HubSpot or Zoho CRM, merging duplicates by email, phone and domain, and record the source and the consent captured on the form.
  • Summarize the request with an LLM into need, deliverables, timeline, stated budget range and missing information, saved as a draft note the owner can edit.
  • Apply the firm's written qualification rules, such as service fit, minimum engagement size, sector exclusions and clashes with current retainers, to suggest a status rather than decide it.
  • Route to the right partner or account lead by service line and region, post an alert in Slack and start a first-response timer.
  • Acknowledge on the channel the prospect used: an email, or a WhatsApp reply within the 24-hour customer service window, with a link to book a discovery call.
  • Escalate unanswered enquiries to the new-business lead before the agreed response time lapses.

Human checkpoint

The partner or new-business lead reviews the summary, confirms or changes the qualification status, and decides whether to schedule a call, refer the prospect elsewhere or decline. The system never sends pricing or commits team capacity.

Enquiries that do not become clients are deleted or anonymized after an agreed period. CRM access is limited to the new-business team and partners.

What we deliver

  • AI summary and routing workflow in n8n
  • Acknowledgement templates for email and WhatsApp
  • Response-time alerts and a weekly source report

How we measure it

  • Median first meaningful response time
  • Enquiry-to-discovery-call rate
  • Qualified enquiries by source
  • Enquiries without an owner after one working day

Proposal and engagement termsStandard4–6 weeks

Proposals and engagement letters from approved libraries

Proposals, statements of work and engagement letters start from the firm's approved templates and rate card. AI drafts narrative sections only where the firm allows it, and a partner edits and approves every document before it goes for signature.

Marketing & creative agencies · Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Partners rebuild proposals and engagement letters from the last similar file, which carries old client names, outdated scope wording and inconsistent fee terms. Agencies and consultancies lose days on largely reusable proposals; law and CA firms skip written terms on smaller matters and later disagree about scope.

Trigger

A qualified opportunity or a cleared matter is marked ready for terms in the CRM or matter register, with scoping notes attached.

How it runs

  • Select the template for the engagement type, such as retainer, project, litigation matter, statutory audit, tax filing or advisory, and fill client, team, timeline and fee fields from the record.
  • Retrieve approved content from the firm's own library, such as methodology sections, team profiles and past scope language, filtered by service line and permission.
  • For agencies and consultancies, have an LLM draft context, approach and plan sections from the scoping notes and retrieved content, marking every generated passage.
  • For law and CA firms, assemble wording only from approved clauses: scope, exclusions, fees, GST, confidentiality and, for audits, the terms auditing standards require in writing.
  • Check for leftover names from other clients, missing exclusions, fee arithmetic and GST treatment, then send the draft to the partner to edit and approve.
  • Send the approved version for e-signature, file the signed copy against the client record and notify the onboarding workflow.

Human checkpoint

The engagement partner edits the draft, sets the final scope and fee, and approves it. Nothing reaches a client without that approval, and AI-drafted text stays highlighted until a person has reviewed it.

  • Partner editing time per draft

Doing the workStandard3–5 weeks

Research synthesis with traceable citations

Consultants get a structured research pack on a market, company or topic, built from permitted sources, with every statement linked to its source and gaps marked for an analyst to verify.

Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Early research for proposals and diagnostics takes analysts days of searching, copying and formatting. AI tools speed this up but produce confident statements with weak or missing sources, which cannot go into a client deliverable.

Trigger

An engagement manager submits a research request with the question, scope, geography, time period and source rules.

How it runs

  • Turn the request into a research plan with sub-questions and a permitted source list: company filings, regulator and government data, industry bodies, licensed databases and client-provided material.
  • Gather results through search APIs and permitted collection, respecting site terms and paywalls, and store each source with its URL and retrieval date.
  • Have an LLM extract claims, figures and quotes into a structured table, each row linked to the source passage.
  • Draft a synthesis that separates sourced findings, conflicting evidence and open questions, with no unsourced figures.
  • Send the pack to the analyst for verification, and save approved findings to the firm's knowledge base for reuse.

Human checkpoint

An analyst checks every figure and quote against its source before use, and the engagement manager decides what goes into client material. Unverified items stay marked as unverified.

  • Company filings and regulator websites

Data & consent

Client-confidential material is kept apart from public research and is never sent to search tools. Sources and retrieval dates are retained with each pack. Collection follows each site's terms and the firm's licenses.

  • Source register with retrieval dates

How we measure it

  • Analyst time per research pack

Dates, status and client updatesStandard3–5 weeks

Weekly client status reports from delivery tools

Each week, work items from Jira or Asana, time logged and agreed campaign results are pulled into a draft status report that the account or engagement lead edits and sends.

Marketing & creative agencies · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Account and engagement leads spend Friday afternoons copying task updates, hours and campaign numbers into slides. Reports arrive late or vary by author, and risks such as slipping deliverables or budget burn come up only when the client asks.

Trigger

A weekly schedule set per client, or a milestone status change in the project tool.

How it runs

  • Pull completed, in-progress and blocked work items for the period from Jira or Asana, with owners and due dates.
  • Add hours against budget from the time tracker and, for agencies, results from Google Ads, Meta Ads and GA4 for the metrics agreed with the client only.
  • Have an LLM draft a plain summary of progress, risks, decisions needed and next week's plan, linking each statement to the underlying item or number.
  • Place the draft in the client's report template in Notion, flagging any metric whose source failed to refresh.
  • After the lead approves, send it by email or post it in the shared channel, and log the report against the project.

Human checkpoint

The account or engagement lead edits the draft, confirms every number and decides which risks and decisions to raise. Nothing is sent to the client automatically.

Doing the workAdvanced6–10 weeks

Knowledge assistant grounded in the firm's own work

Lawyers, CAs and consultants ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn only from the firm's approved precedents, opinions and past deliverables, with citations and matter-level access controls.

Law firms & legal practices · Accounting, tax & CA firms · Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Years of opinions, pleadings, tax positions and deliverables sit in folders that only their authors can find. Public AI tools cannot be given client documents, and answers without sources are of no use to a professional who must sign the advice.

Trigger

A professional asks a question in the assistant inside the firm's workspace, such as Slack, Microsoft Teams or an internal web app.

How it runs

  • Inventory approved sources with the knowledge owner: precedents, opinions, research memos, past deliverables and checklists, excluding drafts and restricted matters.
  • Index documents with metadata for client, matter, practice area, date and access group, mirroring permissions and information barriers from the document system.
  • Retrieve only passages the user may see, and have the model answer strictly from them with citations to document and paragraph.
  • Decline and say so when sources are missing or conflicting, rather than answering from general knowledge.
  • Log questions, sources used and user feedback, and review a sample each month with the knowledge owner.

Human checkpoint

The professional reads the cited sources before relying on anything and remains responsible for the advice. A named knowledge owner approves what is indexed and reviews flagged answers. The assistant never advises clients directly.

Billing, collections and reviewAdvanced5–8 weeks

Utilization, realization and pipeline dashboard

Partners see one current view of staff utilization, realization against standard rates, unbilled work and weighted pipeline, built from timesheets, CRM and finance data with shared definitions.

Management & IT consulting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Consulting leaders plan hiring and staffing from spreadsheets that are a month old. Each practice defines utilization differently, realization is calculated only at year end, and the CRM pipeline does not match what partners report in meetings.

Trigger

A scheduled daily data refresh, plus month-end close in the finance system.

How it runs

  • Agree definitions with partners: available hours, billable and non-billable codes, standard rates, realization and pipeline stages with probabilities.
  • Load timesheets, staffing plans, CRM opportunities and invoices into BigQuery, with dbt models applying the agreed definitions.
  • Reconcile totals with the finance system each month and show a data-quality panel for missing timesheets and unmapped codes.
  • Build Power BI views by practice, partner, client and person, with individual-level detail visible only to managers.
  • Send practice heads a weekly summary of bench capacity, over-allocation and pipeline gaps for the next quarter.

Human checkpoint

Practice heads and the managing partner interpret the numbers and make staffing, pricing and hiring decisions. Definitions change only with their written approval, and no one's performance is judged from the dashboard alone.
